* The course of the seventh biggest river in the world was shifted, as were 50 million tonnes of earth and rock.
* The amount of [concrete](/wiki/Concrete "Concrete") used to build the Itaipu Power Plant would be enough to construct 210 [football](/wiki/Football_(soccer) "Football (soccer)") stadiums the size of the [Estádio do Maracanã](/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_do_Maracan%C3%A3 "Estádio do Maracanã").
* The [iron](/wiki/Iron "Iron") and [steel](/wiki/Steel "Steel") used would allow for the construction of 380 [Eiffel Towers](/wiki/Eiffel_Tower "Eiffel Tower").
* The total volume of excavation of earth and rock in Itaipu is 8.5 times greater than that of the [Channel Tunnel](/wiki/Channel_Tunnel "Channel Tunnel"), while the volume of concrete is 15 times greater.
* Around forty thousand people worked in the construction.[[20]](#cite_note-20)
* Itaipu is one of the [most expensive objects](/wiki/Lists_of_most_expensive_items "Lists of most expensive items") ever built.

Durant was born on September 29, 1988, in [Washington, D.C.](/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C."),[[10]](#cite_note-Reference-10) to Wanda (*née* Durant) and Wayne Pratt. When Durant was an infant, his father deserted the family; Wanda and Wayne eventually divorced, and Durant's grandmother, Barbara Davis, helped raise him. By age 13, Durant's father reentered his life and traveled the country with him to basketball tournaments.[[11]](#cite_note-breen-11)[[12]](#cite_note-12) Durant has a sister, Brianna, and two brothers, Tony and Rayvonne.[[13]](#cite_note-13)

Durant and his siblings grew up in [Prince George's County, Maryland](/wiki/Prince_George%27s_County,_Maryland "Prince George's County, Maryland"), on the eastern outskirts of Washington, D.C.[[14]](#cite_note-14) He was unusually tall from a young age, and reached 6 ft 0 in (1.83 m) in height while still in [middle school](/wiki/Middle_school "Middle school") (age 10–12).[[15]](#cite_note-15) Growing up, Durant wanted to play for his favorite team, the [Toronto Raptors](/wiki/Toronto_Raptors "Toronto Raptors"),[[16]](#cite_note-I_wanted_to_play_for_the_Raptors-16) which included his favorite player, [Vince Carter](/wiki/Vince_Carter "Vince Carter").[[16]](#cite_note-I_wanted_to_play_for_the_Raptors-16) Durant played [Amateur Athletic Union](/wiki/Amateur_Athletic_Union "Amateur Athletic Union") (AAU) basketball for several teams in the [Maryland](/wiki/Maryland "Maryland") area and was teammates with future NBA players [Michael Beasley](/wiki/Michael_Beasley "Michael Beasley"), [Greivis Vásquez](/wiki/Greivis_V%C3%A1squez "Greivis Vásquez"), and [Ty Lawson](/wiki/Ty_Lawson "Ty Lawson"), the first of whom Durant remains friends with to this day.[[17]](#cite_note-Jock-17)[[18]](#cite_note-18) During this time, he began wearing #35 as his jersey number in honor of his AAU coach, Charles Craig, who was murdered at the age of 35.[[19]](#cite_note-19)

One of Barcelona's rivals in European football is Italian club AC Milan.[[215]](#cite_note-215)[[216]](#cite_note-216)[[217]](#cite_note-217)[[218]](#cite_note-218) The team against which Barcelona has played the most matches (19), it is also the third most played match in European club competitions, behind Real Madrid–Juventus (21) and Real Madrid–Bayern Munich (26).[[219]](#cite_note-219)[[220]](#cite_note-220)[[221]](#cite_note-221) Two of the most successful clubs in Europe, Milan has won seven European Cups to Barça's five, while both clubs have won a record five European Super Cups.[[222]](#cite_note-222) Barcelona and Milan have won other continental titles, which make them the second and third most decorated teams in world football, with 19 and 14 titles respectively, both behind Real Madrid's 23.[[223]](#cite_note-223)

Barcelona leads the head-to-head record with eight wins and five defeats. The first encounter between the two clubs was in the [1959–60 European Cup](/wiki/1959%E2%80%9360_European_Cup "1959–60 European Cup"). They faced off in the round of 16 and Barça won the tie on a 7–1 aggregate score (0–2 in Milan and 5–1 in Barcelona).[[224]](#cite_note-224) While Milan had never knocked Barcelona out of the European Cup, they beat Johan Cruyff's Dream Team 4–0 in the [1994 Champions League final](/wiki/1994_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "1994 UEFA Champions League Final"), despite being the underdogs.[[225]](#cite_note-225)[[226]](#cite_note-226) In 2013, however, Barcelona made a "historic" comeback from a 0–2 first leg defeat in the round of 16 of the [2012–13 Champions League](/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_UEFA_Champions_League "2012–13 UEFA Champions League"),

Natalie Coughlin :: part 05 :: chunk_0004
**Natalie Anne Coughlin Hall** (born August 23, 1982) is an American former competition swimmer and twelve-time Olympic medalist. While attending the [University of California, Berkeley](/wiki/University_of_California,_Berkeley "University of California, Berkeley"), she became the first woman ever to swim the [100-meter backstroke](/wiki/World_record_progression_100_metres_backstroke#Long_course_2 "World record progression 100 metres backstroke") (long course) in less than one minute. At the [2008 Summer Olympics](/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics"), she became the first U.S. female athlete in modern Olympic history to win six medals in one Olympiad, and the first woman ever to win a 100-meter backstroke gold in two consecutive Olympics.[[2]](#cite_note-2) At the [2012 Summer Olympics](/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics"), in her third and final Olympic appearance, she earned a bronze medal in the 4×100-meter freestyle relay.

Coughlin's success has earned her the [World Swimmer of the Year Award](/wiki/Swimming_World_Swimmers_of_the_Year "Swimming World Swimmers of the Year") once and [American Swimmer of the Year Award](/wiki/Swimming_World_Swimmers_of_the_Year#American_Swimmer_of_the_Year "Swimming World Swimmers of the Year") three times. She has won a total of 59 medals in major international competition, twenty-five gold, twenty-two silver, and thirteen bronze spanning the Olympics, the [World](/wiki/FINA_World_Aquatics_Championships "FINA World Aquatics Championships"), the [Pan Pacific](/wiki/Pan_Pacific_Swimming_Championships "Pan Pacific Swimming Championships") Championships, and the [Pan American Games](/wiki/Pan_American_Games "Pan American Games").

Bamba was born on May 12, 1998, in [Harlem](/wiki/Harlem "Harlem"), [New York](/wiki/New_York_(state) "New York (state)") to Lancine Bamba and Aminata Johnson, who both emigrated from the [Ivory Coast](/wiki/Ivory_Coast "Ivory Coast").[[2]](#cite_note-bio-2)[[3]](#cite_note-paprep-3)[[4]](#cite_note-bluechip-4) Bamba's grandparents were born and brought up in present-day [Mali](/wiki/Mali "Mali").[[3]](#cite_note-paprep-3) His older brother, Sidiki Johnson, played college basketball at [Arizona](/wiki/Arizona_Wildcats_men%27s_basketball "Arizona Wildcats men's basketball"), [Providence](/wiki/Providence_Friars_men%27s_basketball "Providence Friars men's basketball"), and [Wabash Valley](/wiki/Wabash_Valley_College "Wabash Valley College").[[5]](#cite_note-slam-5) Another member of his family, [estranged](/wiki/Family_estrangement "Family estrangement") brother Ibrahim Johnson, also played college basketball at multiple universities, including both [Farmingdale State](/wiki/Farmingdale_State_College "Farmingdale State College") and [Montevallo](/wiki/Montevallo_Falcons "Montevallo Falcons").[[6]](#cite_note-6)[[7]](#cite_note-7) Bamba first became interested in basketball at age six, inspired by the game's popularity in his hometown.[[3]](#cite_note-paprep-3)

In 2012, 7,950 [wildfires](/wiki/Wildfire "Wildfire") burned a total of 869,599 acres (3,519.14 km2) in the [US state](/wiki/US_state "US state") of [California](/wiki/California "California");[[1]](#cite_note-1): 62 these included the massive [Rush Fire](/wiki/Rush_Fire "Rush Fire"), which was the tenth-largest wildfire recorded in California in modern times, and the [Ponderosa Fire](/wiki/Ponderosa_Fire "Ponderosa Fire"), which destroyed 133 structures. The [California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection](/wiki/California_Department_of_Forestry_and_Fire_Protection "California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection") (Cal Fire) incurred fire suppression costs of US$310 million between July 2012 and June 2013, in addition to wildfire damages of $28.2 million.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

Adams married [Troian Bellisario](/wiki/Troian_Bellisario "Troian Bellisario") (star of *[Pretty Little Liars](/wiki/Pretty_Little_Liars "Pretty Little Liars")*) on December 10, 2016, in [Santa Barbara, California](/wiki/Santa_Barbara,_California "Santa Barbara, California").[[24]](#cite_note-24)[[25]](#cite_note-25)[[26]](#cite_note-26) The two met in 2009 when they were cast opposite each other in the play *Equivocation*,[[27]](#cite_note-27) then broke up briefly but got back together after Adams' guest appearance on *Pretty Little Liars* in 2010.[[28]](#cite_note-28)[[29]](#cite_note-29) They have three daughters, Aurora (born 2018), Elliot (born 2021) and Imogen (born 2026).[[30]](#cite_note-30)[[31]](#cite_note-31)

Adams was awarded Honorary Life Membership of [University College Dublin Law Society](/wiki/University_College_Dublin_Law_Society "University College Dublin Law Society") in September 2013.[[34]](#cite_note-34)[[35]](#cite_note-35)[[36]](#cite_note-36)

He plays the guitar and is an avid photographer who owns more than 25 cameras.[[37]](#cite_note-37)
His photos were featured in *Suits' Behind the Lens* and #PJAGallery exhibitions.[[38]](#cite_note-38)

[Wellington Square](/wiki/Wellington_Square,_Oxford "Wellington Square, Oxford") has become synonymous with the university's central administration.

The university's formal head is the [chancellor](/wiki/List_of_Chancellors_of_the_University_of_Oxford "List of Chancellors of the University of Oxford"), with [Lord Hague of Richmond](/wiki/William_Hague "William Hague") inaugurated in 2025[[100]](#cite_note-100) although, as at most British universities, the chancellor is a titular figurehead and is not involved with the day-to-day running of the university. The chancellor is elected by the members of [convocation](/wiki/Convocation "Convocation"), a body comprising all graduates of the university, and may hold office until death.[[101]](#cite_note-101)

The [vice-chancellor](/wiki/List_of_Vice-Chancellors_of_the_University_of_Oxford "List of Vice-Chancellors of the University of Oxford"), currently [Irene Tracey](/wiki/Irene_Tracey "Irene Tracey"),[[9]](#cite_note-VCapproval-9) is the *de facto* head of the university. There are five pro-vice-chancellors with specific responsibilities.[[102]](#cite_note-102)

Two university [proctors](/wiki/Proctor_of_the_University_of_Oxford "Proctor of the University of Oxford"), elected annually on a rotating basis from any two of the colleges, are the internal ombudsmen who make sure that the university and its members adhere to its statutes. This role incorporates student discipline and complaints, as well as oversight of the university's proceedings.[[103]](#cite_note-103) The university's professors are collectively referred to as the [Statutory Professors of the University of Oxford](/wiki/List_of_professorships_at_the_University_of_Oxford "List of professorships at the University of Oxford"). [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/%D0%A8%D0%B0%D0%B2%D0%BB%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B8%D0%B5_%D0%BE%D0%B7%D1%91%D1%80%D0%B0.jpg/250px-%D0%A8%D0%B0%D0%B2%D0%BB%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B8%D0%B5_%D0%BE%D0%B7%D1%91%D1%80%D0%B0.jpg)](/wiki/File:%D0%A8%D0%B0%D0%B2%D0%BB%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B8%D0%B5_%D0%BE%D0%B7%D1%91%D1%80%D0%B0.jpg)

[Altay Mountains](/wiki/Altay_Mountains "Altay Mountains")

In the mountain system west of [Lake Baikal](/wiki/Lake_Baikal "Lake Baikal") in south-central Siberia, the highest elevations are 3,300 metres (10,800 ft) in the Western [Sayan](/wiki/Sayan_Mountains "Sayan Mountains"), 3,200 metres (10,500 ft) in the Eastern Sayan, and 4,500 metres (14,800 ft) at [Belukha Mountain](/wiki/Belukha_Mountain "Belukha Mountain") in the [Altay Mountains](/wiki/Altay_Mountains "Altay Mountains"). The Eastern Sayan reach nearly to the southern shore of [Lake Baikal](/wiki/Lake_Baikal "Lake Baikal"); at the lake, there is an elevation difference of more than 4,500 metres (14,800 ft) between the nearest mountain, 2,840 metres (9,320 ft) high, and the deepest part of the lake, which is 1,700 metres (5,600 ft) below sea level. The mountain systems east of Lake Baikal are lower, forming a complex of minor ranges and valleys that reaches from the lake to the Pacific coast. The maximum height of the [Stanovoy Range](/wiki/Stanovoy_Range "Stanovoy Range"), which runs west to east from northern Lake Baikal to the Sea of Okhotsk, is 2,550 metres (8,370 ft). To the south of that range is southeastern Siberia, whose mountains reach 800 metres (2,600 ft). Across the [Strait of Tartary](/wiki/Strait_of_Tartary "Strait of Tartary") from that region is [Sakhalin Island](/wiki/Sakhalin "Sakhalin"), Russia's largest island, where the highest elevation is about 1,700 metres (5,600 ft). The small [Moneron Island](/wiki/Moneron_Island "Moneron Island"), the site of the shootdown of [Korean Air Lines Flight 007](/wiki/Korean_Air_Lines_Flight_007 "Korean Air Lines Flight 007"), is found to its west.

Wright brothers :: Early career and research :: part 02 :: chunk_0004
Wilbur said, "Lilienthal was without question the greatest of the precursors, and the world owes to him a great debt."[[33]](#cite_note-airandspace.si.edu-33) In May 1899 Wilbur wrote a letter[[34]](#cite_note-34) to [the Smithsonian Institution](/wiki/The_Smithsonian_Institution "The Smithsonian Institution") requesting information and publications about aeronautics.[[35]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHoward198830-35) Drawing on the work of [Sir George Cayley](/wiki/Sir_George_Cayley "Sir George Cayley"), Chanute, Lilienthal, [Leonardo da Vinci](/wiki/Leonardo_da_Vinci "Leonardo da Vinci"), and Langley, they began their mechanical aeronautical experimentation that year.

The Wright brothers always presented a unified image to the public, sharing equally in the credit for their invention. Biographers note that Wilbur took the initiative in 1899 and 1900, writing of "my" machine and "my" plans before Orville became deeply involved when the first person singular became the plural "we" and "our". Author [James Tobin](/wiki/James_Tobin_(author) "James Tobin (author)") asserts, "it is impossible to imagine Orville, bright as he was, supplying the driving force that started their work and kept it going from the back room of a store in Ohio to conferences with capitalists, presidents, and kings. Will did that. He was the leader, from the beginning to the end."[[36]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETobin200492-36)

The **Italy national football team** ([Italian](/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language"): *Nazionale di calcio dell'Italia*) has represented [Italy](/wiki/Italy "Italy") in men's international [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") since its first match in 1910. The national team is controlled by the [Italian Football Federation](/wiki/Italian_Football_Federation "Italian Football Federation") (FIGC), the governing body for [football in Italy](/wiki/Football_in_Italy "Football in Italy"), which is a co-founder and member of [UEFA](/wiki/UEFA "UEFA"). Italy's home matches are played at various stadiums throughout Italy, and its primary [training ground](/wiki/Training_ground_(association_football) "Training ground (association football)") and technical headquarters, [Centro Tecnico Federale di Coverciano](/wiki/Centro_Tecnico_Federale_di_Coverciano "Centro Tecnico Federale di Coverciano"), is located in [Florence](/wiki/Florence "Florence").

Italy is one of the most successful national teams in international competitions, having won four [World Cup](/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup") titles ([1934](/wiki/1934_FIFA_World_Cup "1934 FIFA World Cup"), [1938](/wiki/1938_FIFA_World_Cup "1938 FIFA World Cup"), [1982](/wiki/1982_FIFA_World_Cup "1982 FIFA World Cup"), [2006](/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup "2006 FIFA World Cup")), reaching two more finals ([1970](/wiki/1970_FIFA_World_Cup "1970 FIFA World Cup"), [1994](/wiki/1994_FIFA_World_Cup "1994 FIFA World Cup")), and finishing third place in [1990](/wiki/1990_FIFA_World_Cup "1990 FIFA World Cup") and fourth in [1978](/wiki/1978_FIFA_World_Cup "1978 FIFA World Cup"). Italy also won two [European Championships](/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship "UEFA European Championship") ([1968](/wiki/UEFA_Euro_1968 "UEFA Euro 1968"), [2020](/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2020 "UEFA Euro 2020")), and appeared in two other finals of the tournament ([2000](/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2000 "UEFA Euro 2000"), [2012](/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2012 "UEFA Euro 2012")). Main article: [2018 Pennsylvania gubernatorial election § Lieutenant Governor](/wiki/2018_Pennsylvania_gubernatorial_election#Lieutenant_Governor "2018 Pennsylvania gubernatorial election")

On November 14, 2017, Fetterman announced that he would run for the Democratic nomination for lieutenant governor of Pennsylvania, challenging, among others, incumbent lieutenant governor [Mike Stack](/wiki/Mike_Stack "Mike Stack").[[52]](#cite_note-:0-52) Stack was seen as a vulnerable incumbent after the Pennsylvania inspector general launched an investigation into Stack regarding allegations that he mistreated his staff and Pennsylvania state troopers.[[53]](#cite_note-53) Fetterman was endorsed by Vermont senator [Bernie Sanders](/wiki/Bernie_Sanders "Bernie Sanders"), Pittsburgh mayor [Bill Peduto](/wiki/Bill_Peduto "Bill Peduto") and former Pennsylvania governor and Philadelphia mayor [Ed Rendell](/wiki/Ed_Rendell "Ed Rendell").[[33]](#cite_note-WAPO2018-33)[[52]](#cite_note-:0-52)[[54]](#cite_note-54) On May 15, Fetterman won the Democratic primary for lieutenant governor with 38% of the vote.[[55]](#cite_note-55) He was a part of the Democratic ticket along with incumbent governor [Tom Wolf](/wiki/Tom_Wolf "Tom Wolf"). On November 6, 2018, Wolf and Fetterman defeated the [Republican](/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") ticket of [Scott Wagner](/wiki/Scott_Wagner "Scott Wagner") and [Jeff Bartos](/wiki/Jeff_Bartos "Jeff Bartos") in the general election.[[56]](#cite_note-56)[[57]](#cite_note-57)[[58]](#cite_note-58)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/85/Alum_Cave_Bluffs_Trail.jpg/250px-Alum_Cave_Bluffs_Trail.jpg)](/wiki/File:Alum_Cave_Bluffs_Trail.jpg)

The [Alum Cave Trail](/wiki/Alum_Cave_Trail "Alum Cave Trail") to the summit of Mount LeConte provides numerous views of the Great Smoky Mountains.

Main article: [Hiking in the Great Smoky Mountains National Park](/wiki/Hiking_in_the_Great_Smoky_Mountains_National_Park "Hiking in the Great Smoky Mountains National Park")

There are 850 miles (1,370 km) of trails and unpaved roads in the park for hiking.

A total of the 71.6 miles (115.2 km) of the [Appalachian Trail](/wiki/Appalachian_Trail "Appalachian Trail") (AT) are located within the park.[[108]](#cite_note-recop-108) The AT enters the park atop Fontana Dam, and ascends a long ridge to the top of Brier Lick Knob at the Tennessee-North Carolina state line. The trail then roughly follows the crest of the range and the state line for its remainder in the park, rarely dropping below 5,000 feet (1,500 m).[[109]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWise2014223–226-109) Kuwohi is the highest point along the entire trail.[[110]](#cite_note-110) Other notable summits that the AT traverses include [Thunderhead Mountain](/wiki/Thunderhead_Mountain "Thunderhead Mountain"), [Silers Bald](/wiki/Silers_Bald "Silers Bald"), [Mount Collins](/wiki/Mount_Collins "Mount Collins"), Newfound Gap, [Mount Kephart](/wiki/Mount_Kephart "Mount Kephart"), [Charlies Bunion](/wiki/Charlies_Bunion "Charlies Bunion"), [Mount Sequoyah](/wiki/Mount_Sequoyah "Mount Sequoyah"), [Mount Chapman](/wiki/Mount_Chapman "Mount Chapman"), [Mount Guyot](/wiki/Mount_Guyot_(Great_Smoky_Mountains) "Mount Guyot (Great Smoky Mountains)"), [Old Black](/wiki/Old_Black_(Great_Smoky_Mountains) "Old Black (Great Smoky Mountains)"), and [Mount Cammerer](/wiki/Mount_Cammerer "Mount Cammerer"). A total of 12 trail shelters are located along the Appalachian Trail in the park, which are used mostly for extended backpacking trips.[[109]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWise2014223–226-109)
